I've saved the workbook to `/home/uctpiaj/work/extraction/medivation.xlsx`. It has the four sheets in the required order, with frozen headers, filters, wrapped text, real dates in MM/DD/YYYY format and no merged cells. A script check confirmed that every quotation appears word for word on the page it cites and is at most 30 words. It also confirmed that sort dates never go backwards and that every flag matches a Question or Review item.

**What the ledger shows (26 rows, one sale process, two rounds):**
- **Before round 1:** Sanofi sent an unsolicited, non-binding offer of $52.50 per share, received 04/15/2016. It was made public 04/28 and rejected 04/29. Pfizer said it was interested on 05/02.
- **Round 1:** opens 06/28/2016, when Medivation's bankers (J.P. Morgan and Evercore) contacted Pfizer. Pfizer signed a confidentiality agreement on 06/29. By 07/05, Medivation had announced confidentiality agreements with "several parties," including Sanofi. Pfizer made an informal bid of $65.00 in cash on 08/08.
- **Round 2:** opens 08/10/2016, when Pfizer and "several other interested parties" were invited to a further round. I coded the round as announced as final. Pfizer made formal bids of $77.00 on 08/19 and a "best and final" $81.50 on 08/20, and the agreement was signed that afternoon.
- **The auction screen is met:** at least two parties signed confidentiality agreements. I classed the process as bidder-led, because Sanofi's approach came first.

**Limits of this filing:**
- **It's Pfizer's tender-offer document, so it describes only Pfizer's side.** It reports no bids from Sanofi or the other parties after July, and it doesn't say how many "several" is. So under the instruction's default rules, two exits are inferred rather than reported:
  - Sanofi is coded as dropped on 08/10, because it isn't named among the round-2 invitees.
  - The unnamed parties are coded as not submitting a bid by the 08/19 due date.
- **There's no fairness opinion to check against.** That would be in Medivation's own response filing (Schedule 14D-9), which wasn't supplied. The $81.50 price matches the merger-agreement summary.
- **Sanofi's type is Unknown,** because the filing never describes what kind of company it is and the instruction rules out outside knowledge.

**Open points for review (Questions sheet):**
- **Q1:** whether the round-2 invitees are the same parties that signed confidentiality agreements in round 1.
- **Q2:** whether the 08/14 request for a "definitive proposal" made round 2 final. If not, the "best and final" request starts a round 3.
- **Q3:** whether Pfizer's promise to sell off "certain products" if competition regulators require it should count as a regulatory concern on its formal bids.

Review items R1–R6 cover the remaining judgement calls the instruction asks to be logged.
